messages:
jun: Heads-up — bringing OrpheusX-lite (int4) online. After conversion we see a headwise rotary ordering mismatch: attention aligns fine for heads 0-7, then from head ~8 the key/value indices look swapped and the KV cache drifts after a few tokens. Context len 512. Dropping quick triage notes here.
claire: Can you paste the conversion command, the vocab-map you used, and a small tokenmap sample? :eyes: 
jun: Ran standard conversion pipeline: 
```
python tools/convert_model.py \
  --src orpheusx \
  --dst gemma \
  --quant int4 \
  --vocab-map maps/orpheusx_to_gemma_v3.json \
  --out /tmp/orp_gemma_int4
```
Tokenmap sample (first 8 ids):
```
{"0":"0","1":"1","2":"2","3":"5","4":"4","5":"3","6":"6","7":"7"}
# note local swap around ids 3-5
```
mateo: That tokenmap swap could be a red flag, but more likely the head layout changed in upstream weights export. Did the exporter interleave heads (like qwen-style) vs contiguous gemma layout?
jun: I dumped the rotary Q/K matrices (fp32 pre-quant) and compared by head index. Patterns show an interleave: (0,2,1,3,4,6,5,7, ...) — consistent with an exporter that wrote even heads first.
sara: For a quick patch, we applied a remap last cycle that fixed Nova->Gemma interleave. Try reordering heads before quantization.
jun: I implemented a small reorder and re-ran the int4 conversion. Permutation generator I used (python):
```
H = num_heads
perm = []
for i in range(H):
    if i % 2 == 0:
        perm.append(i//2)
    else:
        perm.append((H//2) + (i//2))
# apply: tensor = tensor[perm]
```
mateo: Slightly different from our previous one but logically equivalent for even H. Did you apply to rotary & attention proj tensors (q,k,v,o)?
jun: Applied to rotary, q/k/v/o, and layernorm affine order. Results: before reorder int4 ppl on conv-eval = 2.58, fp16 baseline = 1.92. After reorder pre-quant -> int4 ppl = 1.98. So structural head-order was the main regression.
claire: Nice. Can you include a small assert in conversion CI that checks attention-position correlation on a 16-token seed? If correlation drops >5%, fail the build. Also add model-catalog metadata: "head_order": "interleaved" or "contiguous" so onboarding knows what to expect.
jun: Will do. Plan for PR:
- add --head-order flag to convert tool (auto-detect + explicit override)
- tools/check_head_alignment.py that diffs attention position maps and emits a heatmap png
- CI unit test using seed prompt "Hello world" (16 tokens) against a reference fp16 pass
- update maps/orpheusx_to_gemma_v3.json with a note about local token swap 
I will open PR and link logs.
ops-bot: ticket INF-3001 created: "OrpheusX-lite: head-order interleave causing KV-cache drift" assigned to jun, priority P2.
claire: Also add a short note in the model onboarding checklist: run head-order detect + dump first 8 rotary heads before shipping.
jun: Yep — adding checklist item and a small conversion smoke script. Thanks :thumbsup:
